User: Hi, we saw your service. Our intake calls after hours keep going to voicemail.
Agent: Got it — after-hours intake calls are hitting voicemail. What made you start looking to fix it right now?

Agent: Makes sense — improving client conversion by answering those after-hours intake calls. When those calls go to voicemail, do they usually leave a message, or do they just call the next place?
User: They usually leave a message, but many might book if someone answered directly.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense—people are ready to book in the moment. Roughly how many after-hours calls hit voicemail in a typical week?
User: About 12 calls a week go to voicemail after hours.
Agent: Got it — about 12 after-hours calls a week are going to voicemail. What kind of business is this for (what industry)?
User: It's for a personal injury law firm.
Agent: Got it — personal injury, that after-hours window is huge for intake. When those 12 calls leave a message, how often do you actually end up connecting with them later?
User: About 70% would likely book if someone answered right away.
Agent: Got it — about 70% would likely book if you answered live. What’s your average case value to the firm (just a rough ballpark number)?
User: The average intake value for our firm is about $1,800.
Agent: Got it. If you booked even 70% of those 12 missed after-hours calls, that’s about $15119 extra a week… and that’s just one week—about $65400 over a month; does that sound about right?
User: Yes, that's correct. Improving conversion on those missed calls could significantly boost our revenue.
Agent: Cool — it’s a 20-minute walkthrough where Jay will show you exactly how we catch those after-hours intakes and what the math looks like for your firm. What’s better for you for a quick live call this week — later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow works better for me.
Agent: Perfect — to get it scheduled, what’s your first name?
User: I'm Marcus Bell from Bell & Associates Legal.
Agent: Got it, Marcus Bell with Bell & Associates Legal. And is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you?
User: No, the best contact number is +19172120001.
Agent: Got it — best number is 917-212-0001. And which time zone are you in — Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: We are in the Eastern time zone.
Agent: Perfect — I can get you in as soon as 11:00 AM or 11:45 AM Eastern time tomorrow. Which works?
User: 11:45 AM Eastern time tomorrow works for me. Please book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks — I’m retrying that booking now.
Agent: I’m having trouble confirming the calendar for 11:45 AM Eastern — it’s showing a conflict on our side. Can you do 12:30 PM Eastern instead?
User: Sure, I'll wait. Thank you for confirming the time for the live call.
Agent: Makes sense — I’m not able to confirm 11:45 AM on the calendar right now, so it isn’t booked yet. Can you do 12:30 PM Eastern tomorrow?
User: Yes, book it for 12:30 PM Eastern tomorrow.
Agent: One moment while I lock in 12:30 PM Eastern tomorrow.
Agent: I’ve got the calendar hold, but before I can fully confirm it I need to re-check your best callback number in E.164 format — is it **+19172120001**?
User: Thank you. I'll be available at 12:30 PM Eastern tomorrow for the live call.
Agent: Got it. Just to fully confirm the booking, can you reply with your best callback number exactly as **+1** then the number (for example **+19172120001**)?
User: +19172120001
Agent: Thanks — I have **+19172120001**. Can you also share the best email to send the calendar invite to?
User: Please send the calendar invite to info@bellandassociateslegal.com. Thank you.
Agent: Thanks, Marcus! You’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details — you can add it to your calendar in one click, or reschedule if you need to. Is there anything else I can help you with?
